body:
# the contributor audit: symmetric truncation and all pyramid menus

Source: `candidate 2be89ee8039bb5fd`, Sections 1–5. Full read and independent algebraic audit: PASS for the stated ordinary continuous results. This is not a proof of OC or of an arbitrary-body stationary-section theorem.

For an even unimodal density, normalized layer cake is a probability mixture of uniform laws on centered intervals. If a layer has radius r and the positive truncation is T, its captured mass is (1+x)/2 with x=min(T/r,1); therefore E x=2v−1 exactly. With k=1−v, direct integration of the exponent-two trial denominator gives

    I_k(x)=x(1+x)/[2(1−k)(x+k)],  r>=T.

For r<T the integral is 1/[1−(kr/T)^2]<=I_k(1). Polynomial division gives I_k''(x)=−k/(x+k)^3. Jensen gives I_k(2v−1)=(2v−1)/v. The denominator is positive on the entire captured support. The exponent comparison is valid for both signs of s: the logarithmic derivative in p is −log(1+a/p)+(a/p)/(1+a/p)<=0 for a>−2 and p>=2. Thus the displayed trial c_p=−2(1−v)/(pT) proves the upper bound for every p>=2, without optimizing over an unproved set.

For a centrally symmetric m-body D, its one-dimensional volume density is even and unimodal by the actual section inclusion and Brunn–Minkowski. The upper projective-energy bound follows with p=m+1. The lower bound follows from Jensen on the symmetric core A∩(−A), whose volume is (2v−1)|D|. Hence

    2v−1 <= E_A(0)/|D| <= (2v−1)/v.

The m=1 check is exact: for D=[−1,1], A=[−1,t], the minimizing denominator coefficient is (t−1)/(2t), and E_A(0)=4t/(1+t). Thus v/(1+E_A/|D|)=v²/(3v−1), minimized at v=2/3 with value 4/9.

The pyramid formulas were checked in ray coordinates (X,z)=(s b,H−(H+1)s). Rays with a·b>1 are completely captured; omitting them would invalidate the result. On the remaining rays the captured scale is H/(H+1−a·b). This gives exactly

    p_a=1−v+(H/d)C_a.

The section map X=H b/(H+1−a·b) has Jacobian H^(d−1)(H+1)/(H+1−a·b)^d. Its centroid is zero precisely when the derivative of the projective energy vanishes at l=−a/(H+1). That parameter is strictly admissible. Convexity of the energy then proves C_a/C_0=E_A(0)/|D|; no assumed projective monotonicity is used.

Finally put e=C_a/C_0. The energy bounds imply 1/(2−e)<=v<=(1+e)/2 and 0<e<=1. The two elementary comparisons in Section 5 give

    4/9 <= v−4e/9 <=5/9.

Consequently the SAME scalar correction c_*=(p_0−4/9)/C_0 works for every actual centroidal section, regardless of its direction or cap mass. Opposite orientations retain the interval [4/9,5/9]; vertical caps have fraction 1/2 and zero correction. Coarea-weighted normal balance cancels the correction exactly. This proves the full-family pyramid theorem, including rank greater than two and redundant menus. The triangle at its centroid checks sharpness of 4/9 across the class.

There is no lattice transformation in this argument. Ordinary continuous coordinates are used only on an ordinary body. There is no claimed reduction from general bodies to these pyramids, nor a claimed payment for mixed families whose actual sections involve other fibers.
